title: Fundamental Review of the Trading Book (FRTB)

maps.tested: Eight sources, and multiple recalls independently give the same count: 2-3 questions per sitting. Both third-party sheets mark the whole chapter important. Rising sharply in weight since 2021.
maps.specifics: Reported angles: the ES-replaces-VaR shift and why; liquidity horizons by asset class; the standardised approach vs. internal models approach; trading-book / banking-book boundary; and comparative questions framed as 'FRTB vs Basel 1, Basel 2, Basel 2.5: overall changes'. One source flags 'refer GARP for Curve Risk' specifically, i.e. the curvature risk charge is not well covered in condensed notes.

vardeezReading: MR-18: Very Important, "Again Full chapter is IMP (Refer GARP for Curve Risk)". ORR-21: untiered in his sheet, but his theme "Basel III: three components and comparison with Basel I and II" draws on this reading. ORR-22: untiered (tier cell reads 0), but his themes "Stressed market VaR (calculations)" and "Basel 2.5 market risk calculation" land squarely here, so treat as high priority.

los.vardeez: Stressed VaR calculation; Basel 2.5 market risk calculation

selectors.name: Stressed ES 97.5% replaces 99% VaR
selectors.what: FRTB replaces the 10-day 99% VaR of Basel I and Basel 2.5 with stressed expected shortfall at 97.5%, based on how market variables moved in stressed conditions, and asks why. For normal losses 99% VaR = mu + 2.326 sigma and 97.5% ES = mu + 2.338 sigma, almost the same; for heavier tails 97.5% ES can be considerably greater than 99% VaR.

selectors.name: Liquidity horizons and the cascade ES
selectors.what: Liquidity horizons of 10, 20, 40, 60 and 120 days (categories 1 to 5) assigned to risk factors by asset class, and the cascade ES = sqrt(ES1^2 + ES2^2 + 2 ES3^2 + 2 ES4^2 + 6 ES5^2), where ESj shocks only the categories j to 5 over overlapping 10-day stressed changes and the weights come from (LHj - LHj-1)/10 = 1, 1, 2, 2, 6.
selectors.theory: Why the horizon is set by the liquidity of each risk factor rather than fixed at 10 days; why the increments (LHj - LHj-1) and a root-sum-of-squares are used (independence of successive periods, an extension of the square-root rule) and not LHj/10 or a linear sum; a desk with no category 1 factors has ES2 = ES1; the number of ES runs (5 per desk).

selectors.name: Standardized vs internal models, desk tests
selectors.what: The two FRTB approaches: the standardized approach is always calculated and acts as a floor, internal models permission is granted desk by desk, and a desk drops to the standardized approach on failing the backtest (1-day VaR over 12 months: more than 12 exceptions at 99% or more than 30 at 97.5%) or the P&L attribution tests (Mean(U)/SD(V) within -10% to +10%, Var(U)/Var(V) below 20%, four or more breaches in 12 months).

selectors.name: Trading book / banking book boundary
selectors.what: How FRTB draws the line between the trading book (market risk capital) and the banking book (credit risk capital): intent to trade is no longer enough, the bank must be able to trade and manage the risks on a desk, assignment is at initiation, and transfers are allowed only in extraordinary circumstances with any capital benefit disallowed.

selectors.name: FRTB vs Basel I, II, 2.5: overall changes
selectors.what: Which change belongs to which accord: Basel I 1996 Amendment (10-day 99% VaR, multiplier m >= 3, backtest exceptions raise m), Basel II (IRB, operational risk, three pillars, market risk unchanged), Basel 2.5 (stressed VaR, incremental risk charge, comprehensive risk measure), and what FRTB changes against them (one stressed ES, liquidity horizons, desk-level approval, standardized floor, firmer book boundary).

selectors.name: Curvature risk charge
selectors.what: The standardized charge for gamma risk: shock factor i up and down by its risk weight Wi, take the delta-predicted change less the actual change in each direction, charge = max(Wi delta_i - dV+, -Wi delta_i - dV-, 0). Short options attract the charge; long options give zero.
selectors.theory: Why curvature is measured as delta-implied versus actual revaluation, why short options lose from curvature and long options gain, why the greater of the two directions is used and a negative result counts as zero, and how a term structure is shifted in parallel by the largest Wi.

notSelected: The sensitivity-based delta and vega charge calculation, the default risk charge, the residual risk add-on, the IMA capital formula with non-modelable risk factors, and the credit-spread and securitization treatment within MR-18 c have no selector, and the Basel 2.5 stressed VaR and incremental risk or comprehensive risk calculations (ORR-22 a, b, c) are covered here only as accord attributions in S5, their calculations belonging to D4.
